content.overview: Muslim personal law in India covers nikah (civil contract with religious significance), dower (mahr), forms of divorce, judicial dissolution under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 on instantaneous triple talaq. Always name the statute. Shayara Bano held talaq-e-biddat unconstitutional; the 2019 Act declares instantaneous triple talaq void and illegal.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Nikah essentials? (2) Mahr? (3) Talaq path or DMMA s. 2? (4) Instant triple talaq — Shayara Bano + 2019 Act?
content.study:
Nikah: ijab and qubul at the same meeting; competent parties; free consent; absence of prohibited relationship; witnesses under Sunni law as commonly applied.

Mahr: specified or unspecified; prompt or deferred; a debt and protection for the wife.

Divorce: classical modes; wife’s judicial path under DMMA s. 2; instant triple talaq void/illegal under 2019 Act after Shayara Bano.

Case already in migrated file: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017) 9 SCC 1. No additional cases invented.
